import pandas as pd,numpy as np,json
from scipy.spatial.distance import pdist
a=pd.read_csv('assemblage.tsv',sep='\t',index_col=0);p=pd.read_csv('picking.csv',index_col=0)
print(a.sum(axis=1).values)
c=a.div(a.sum(axis=1),axis=0).mul(p.n_picked.loc[a.index],axis=0)
print(c.round(2).values[:3])
m=pdist(c.values,'braycurtis').mean();m2=pdist(a.values,'braycurtis').mean();print(m,m2)
json.dump({"status":"completed_with_assumptions","results":{"mean_bray_curtis":float(m)},
"assumptions":["Percentages converted to raw counts as percent/100 * n_picked (rows renormalised by their sums, which are ~100)."],
"exclusions":[],"issues":["assemblage.tsv holds percentages, not raw counts; reconstructed counts using picking.csv. Rounding of percentages makes counts approximate. Using percentages directly would give %.6f."%m2],
"summary":"Reconstructed counts from percentages and n_picked, computed Bray-Curtis for all 36 sample pairs, and averaged."},open('answer.json','w'))
